title: Godotite - Nanite-inspired continuous LOD for Godot
author: Arkaein
selftext:
I just released Godotite, a continuous LOD system for Godot inspired by Unreal Engine 5's Nanite. Was developed mainly with Claude code.

[https://github.com/Arkaein/godotite](https://github.com/Arkaein/godotite)

It's intended for very large meshes that more traditional heightmap-based terrain methods like Geometry Clipmaps can't handle: sheer cliffs, caves, other overlapping geometry.

This video shows the included demo, flying over a generated terrain, showing the transitions between seamless clusters at different levels of detail.

Designed to be easy to use, it provides an import feature where any imported model can be converted into an LOD structure with a single checkbox and reimport. Also supports scene tree nodes for creating LODs within the editor, most useful for procedurally generated geometry.

This is only a \*partial\* implementation of Nanite. Most notably no streaming, so a mesh and materials should be a size that fits within memory, but is too large to render with high performance. Streaming may be added in the future, but I don't have a test case in my own project.

This Goldilocks zone is something like millions to tens of millions of triangles. Much less won't show much speedup, and performance will be bottlenecked by fragment shading.

Godotite uses standard Godot rendering, no custom software rasterizer like Nanite. All normal materials and shaders should work, though meshes with large numbers of surfaces and materials will not optimize as well as meshes with a small number of materials covering very large patches.
